The little bar chart under each post gives you impressions, engagements, profile visits, and link clicks. It’s useful, but it’s only a snapshot. The real insight comes from spotting patterns across posts — which formats get seen, which topics get replies, and what you posted right before your follower count jumped.
That's what Twitter analytics is for, and in this guide I’ll show you where to find each number on a free X account, on Premium, and in Buffer Insights, and how to read them.

X native analytics vs. Buffer: which Twitter analytics tool is right for you?

Twitter analytics — now called X analytics — is X's built-in reporting on how your posts and account are performing. It covers post-level numbers like impressions, engagements, link clicks, and profile visits, plus account-level trends like engagement rate over time and follower growth.
Every account can see post-level numbers:
But the full account dashboard, including audience demographics, needs an X Premium subscription.
This bummed me out, until I learned that Buffer Insights shows your X analytics, like impressions, engagement rate, and follower growth, on the free plan.

Whichever route you take, these numbers show how your posts and account are performing: reach, engagement, and follower changes. With X Premium, you also get better insights into your audience demographics.
Together, they can help you shape your social media strategy — what to post, when to post, and which topics your audience cares about.
How to check your Twitter (X) analytics
There are three ways to see your X analytics:
On any account: basic insights for each post
With X Premium: the full analytics dashboard
With Buffer: your X analytics, free, in Buffer Insights
Here’s how each one works, starting with the one you already have.

Number of likes, reposts, and comments

The catch is that you only get one post at a time. There’s no account-level view and no way to spot patterns across posts, unless you’re up for a lot of spreadsheet math (ugh). That’s what X Premium is for.

Premium is useful, but it isn’t the right call for everyone. It’s a paid subscription, and it only shows you analytics for the one X account you’re logged into.
If you’d rather not pay for it (like me), or you want your X numbers next to your other channels, a tool like Buffer is perfect.

The best part about using Buffer over native analytics — at least for me — is that I get to do everything related to my social media efforts in one tab. I can find post ideas, create content, schedule posts, reply to people, check analytics, and pull my weekly takeaways without switching tools.

Let’s break these down one by one, so you know what to do with each number once you’ve found it.
1. Use impressions to understand what's getting your content seen
Impressions measure how many times someone saw your posts — it could be in the feed or search results. Watch this metric closely if you’re trying to build more awareness for your personal brand.
A jump in impressions usually has a reason behind it. It could be one of these:
Timing: You posted when your audience was actually scrolling.
Format: A post in one format (like a video) caught attention in ways a text or image post didn't.
Topic: You posted about something people were already searching for, something timely, or something your audience normally responds to.
High engagement: An earlier post picked up reposts, shares, or comments and drew more people to your account.

Look for patterns across post impressions. Do video posts consistently get thousands of impressions while text posts get a couple of hundred? Do Tuesday morning posts outperform Friday afternoon? That tells you what's worth repeating.
Look at impressions over time, not just for individual posts. Zooming out helps you understand whether your X strategy is actually working out or whether you’re getting a few lucky hits.
Where to find impressions in X
On the Account Overview dashboard in X analytics, you'll see total impressions for the selected period and a chart of impressions over time.
You can layer other metrics onto that chart to learn more.
Compare impressions to engagement rate to see whether your posts are reaching people and getting them to interact
Or compare them to new followers to see whether visibility is turning into follower growth

What about seeing impressions for individual posts? Click the Content tab in your X analytics dashboard. You can click any post there to see more detailed impressions data for the first 48 hours after posting.
You can also see post-level impressions for free by clicking on the bar chart at the bottom right of each post.
Where to find impressions in Buffer
In Buffer Insights, the X/Twitter dashboard shows impressions per post and for the selected period.
2. Use engagement rate to find which posts drive the most engagement

Engagement rate tells you what percentage of people who saw your post actually interacted with it. A high engagement rate means people stopped scrolling and did something — liked, replied, shared, or clicked.

Comparing engagement rates across post types shows you which formats work best for your audience. In Buffer’s data on content formats, text posts on X earn the highest median engagement rate at 3.56%, with images close behind (3.40%). Video comes in next, and posts with links come last.
Treat that as a starting point, not a rule. If images consistently pull higher engagement than other types on your account, lean into visual-first posts.
Read more: Social Media Engagement: 9 Ways to Boost Yours + Why it Matters

Breaking engagement down further shows you how people interact with your content. One person can do several of these on the same post. They might like it, repost it, and click through to your profile. Here’s what each type of engagement usually tells you:
Likes: The lightest-touch signal. They’re easy to give, so they show a post landed but not how much it mattered to people.
Replies: People had something to say. This is the closest X gets to a conversation.
Reposts and quote posts: People thought your post was worth passing on to their own followers. A quote post adds their own take on top.
Link clicks: People were curious enough to leave X and read more.
Detail expands: People opened the post to see more, like the full text, the replies or the rest of the thread.
Media engagements: People opened your image or played your video.
Profile clicks: People wanted to know who you are, which often comes before a follow.
Once you spot which engagement types happen most often — and on which posts — you know which formats, tones, or topics to repeat.
Where to find engagement rate in X

The Content tab on the X analytics dashboard shows a table of your posts with impressions, likes, replies, and reposts. Click a post to see its total engagement rate and engagement metrics for the first 48 hours after posting.
Download the CSV file from the Content tab for more types of post engagement, like bookmarks, shares, profile visits, detail expands, link clicks, and hashtag clicks.
Where to find engagement rate in Buffer
Your Buffer Insights dashboard shows engagement rate and individual engagement metrics, like reposts, likes, and link clicks, for each post.
You can download the CSV file to analyze the raw data yourself, or check the weekly takeaways, which summarize what changed and suggest what to try next.
3. Evaluate engagement over time against your goals

Engagement rate gets more useful when you watch it over time. One good week doesn’t tell you much. A steady climb (or a slow slide) over a month shows whether what you’re doing is actually moving you toward your goals.
Say you’re trying to build a community on X. To check whether you’re succeeding, evaluate whether the replies you get are rising along with your engagement rate over a few weeks.
More replies mean people are talking back to you (yay!)
Fewer replies are a hint to try different kinds of posts, like questions or opinions, that give people something to respond to
And don’t forget your side of the conversation. In Buffer’s analysis of replies across six platforms, X posts where the creator replied to comments saw around 8% more engagement.
Where to find engagement over time in X
The account overview dashboard shows your engagement rate over time. Add metrics like replies or reposts to see which ones are rising with it.
Where to find engagement over time in Buffer
Check the overview dashboard in Buffer Insights for a summary of engagement rate over time. You can adjust the time period and the period you'd like to compare it to.

And if replying is part of your plan, you can do that in Buffer too. Buffer Community pulls the comments from your connected channels into one dashboard, so you can reply right there instead of opening each app.

Posting randomly on X can get you the odd viral hit (I swear absolutely bonkers things go viral on there!). But throwing spaghetti at the wall only works so often, so you need a concrete goal to give your posts some direction.
But X analytics are more jumpy than I am on four cups of coffee, so comparing one week to the next can be misleading. Thankfully, averages smooth those jumps out.
So instead of judging individual days or posts, compare your average post performance this month with last month.
You can also check your averages against broader benchmarks. Here’s what the benchmark data shows:
Median posting frequency: about 9 posts a month (roughly 2 a week)

Treat these as a rough yardstick, because X as a platform changes with the wind. If your averages are below them, you know where to focus. If they’re higher, you’re outperforming the typical X account.

6. Use follower analytics to spot what's driving growth
When you look at your follower growth chart, check:

Is there an unusually tall day? If so, what did you post in the 24 to 48 hours before it? One post may have resonated, picked up lots of engagement, and helped drive the spike. It could be a one-off, so try a few similar posts and see if you get the same result.
Does a certain content format line up with follower growth? Text, video, or visuals: see if one keeps showing up before your best days.
Do any content pillars or topics get more engagement, and then more followers? Those are the subjects to lean into when you brainstorm content ideas.
Looking at the trend rather than the total helps you double down on what works and rethink what stalls growth.

Psst... consistent posting is the bedrock of growing your followers on any platform. Buffer’s analysis also found our consistent heroes get the reward of five times more engagement per post than people who posted in bursts and vanished. So the tortoise really does beat the hare.
Where to find follower growth data in X
On the X account overview dashboard, the Follows over time chart shows daily counts of new followers and unfollows.

Use the comparative chart to layer new followers with metrics like impressions, profile visits, reposts, and engagement rate. That makes it easier to match spikes in your follower count to the posts or campaigns running at the time.
Where to find follower growth data in Buffer
In the left sidebar, select your X channel, then click Insights beneath the channel name.

The Metrics chart on your dashboard shows Followers by default, so you’ll see how your follower count has moved over your chosen date range. Insights shows the last 30 days to begin with, and you can change that with the date range options at the top.
My favorite hack is to organize my content pillars into tags and see which one(s) bring me the most followers.
If you’ve only just connected your X account, Buffer pulls in a limited amount of past data, so older history may be missing.
7. Use audience insights to check if you're reaching the right people
X's Audience tab shows the age, gender, country, follower status, active times, and devices of the people seeing your posts.
Whether they're a follower or not
The devices they use — X's iOS or Android apps, the web app, or something else

When you compare this data with the audience you want to reach, you can see whether your content is attracting the right people or drifting toward a different group of X users. If they match, keep doing what you’re doing. If they don’t, here’s what to look at:

Location: If most of your audience is in a country you’re not targeting, check your content first. Language, local references, and topics can all pull in a different crowd. If you are targeting that region but it’s in a different time zone, use the active times chart to schedule your posts for when they’re online.

Age: If your audience skews older or younger than your target audience, look at which posts that age group engages with. That shows you what’s attracting them, and whether to lean into it or adjust your topics and tone.

Followers vs. non-followers: If most of the people your posts reach don’t follow you, your content is traveling beyond your existing audience, which is good for discovery. If it’s mostly followers, you’re mostly talking to the same people, so try topics and formats that are easier to share.
Devices: If most of your audience is on mobile, make sure your posts read well on a small screen, with short lines and images that aren’t packed with tiny text.

Changes over time: If your audience mix shifts after you try a new content direction, you’re attracting a different segment. Decide whether that’s the segment you want, then keep going or switch back.

Audience data is also handy if you work with brands. You can check whether your audience lines up with the partners or sponsors you'd like to collaborate with, and use the numbers to strengthen your media kit.
Where to find audience insights in X
To find your audience demographics, simply go to the Audience tab in the X analytics dashboard.
You'll also find audience insights for individual posts in the Content tab, which shows who each post reached.
Buffer doesn't offer audience demographics for X yet, but X analytics gives you plenty to work with as you shape your strategy.
If X has analytics, where does Buffer fit in?

Both X and Buffer give you useful data about how your posts perform. If X is the only place you post and you already pay for Premium, you may not need anything else. Buffer's analytics earn their place in four situations:
If you want Twitter analytics (and true insights) without paying for X Premium
Putting analytics behind a paywall was an interesting call by X, and I’m not sure it worked out quite how they hoped.

In March 2026, SpaceX’s IPO filing put X at about 550 million monthly active users, and only about 4.4 million people were paying X Premium or Premium+ subscribers. That’s under 1% of X’s users, so only a small slice of accounts can see the full account-level dashboard. Oof.
Buffer's analytics cover most of that gap on its free plan. You get nearly the same data you'd find in X's native analytics without paying for X Premium.

But the best part is Buffer also does some of the number-crunching for you. The Insights dashboard pulls patterns out of your data and suggests what to try next, so you can spend your time on your content and your audience instead of spreadsheets. If you want to dig deeper, the raw data is always available to download.
If you post on more than one platform
My favorite benefit of all: With Buffer, I can build one cohesive social media strategy across platforms and see how it’s performing without pulling my hair out.
X Premium is plenty when all you want to know is how you’re doing on X. But really, who’s putting all their (social media) eggs in one basket?
Instead of checking three to five different platforms, working out how you’re doing on each, and then scratching your head over whether you’re actually making progress, you can just… use Buffer.
Open the All Channels view in Insights, and you’ll see how every connected channel is performing in one place.
A few minutes of dashboard surfing, and you have all your answers.
If you need to share X results in a report
X’s native analytics don’t include a report builder. On X Premium, you can download post data from the Content tab, but you’ll still have to turn it into charts and slides yourself. Welp.

In Buffer, you can export your Insights view as a branded PDF to share with your manager, client, or brand partner. Set the channel (or the All Channels view) and the date range you want first, because the PDF reflects whatever you’re looking at.
If you want to run your whole social media workflow in one place
Analytics are only one piece of a social media routine. You also need ideas, content, a schedule, and time to talk to your audience. Buffer covers all of that in one dashboard. You can:
Save and develop post ideas in Create
Plan and schedule posts across your channels in Publish
Reply to comments from all your channels in Community
Get help writing and repurposing posts with the AI Assistant

That all-in-one setup is priceless when you’re juggling even two social media channels. You don’t have to hop between tabs, or keep 375 more open in your head, to remember what’s scheduled, what’s posted, and who you still need to reply to.
Buffer’s free plan covers up to three channels, so you can try the whole workflow before paying for anything.

Hey, if X is your one true love and all you care about is growing on X, go ahead and buy that Premium subscription.

But if you’re posting across a few platforms, or you’d rather keep your money (and skip the Premium subscription), Buffer shows your X analytics for free, right next to everything else you post. Oh, and you can also do literally everything else in your social media workflow using the tool.

Are Twitter (X) analytics free, or do you need Premium?

Basic analytics are free. Any X account can tap the bar chart icon below a post to see its impressions, engagements, profile visits, link clicks, detail expands, replies, and reposts. The full account dashboard — account overview, Audience tab, Content tab, and CSV export — requires an X Premium subscription. If you want account-level trends without Premium, Buffer's free plan shows X post analytics too.
How do I check my Twitter (X) analytics?

On the web, X Premium users can go to x.com/i/account_analytics. On mobile, Premium users tap Premium, then Analytics. Free X users can tap the bar chart icon below any post to see its impressions and engagements. In Buffer, you'll find X analytics under Insights.
Why can't I see my Twitter analytics?

The most common reasons are that you don't have X Premium (needed for the account dashboard), you're not logged in, your account is restricted or suspended, or X is having an outage. Even without the dashboard, you can usually still see post-level numbers by tapping the bar chart icon below a post.
Can you see Twitter analytics for another account?

Not through X's native analytics, which only show data for accounts you own or manage. You can see public counts — views, likes, and reposts — on anyone's posts. For deeper analysis of another account, you'd need a third-party profile analyzer or competitor-tracking tool.
What metrics matter most in X analytics?

The most useful metrics depend on your goals, but impressions, engagement rate, and follower growth are a strong starting point. Together, they show whether your content is being seen, getting interaction, and driving long-term growth.
What does "detail expands" mean on X?

Detail expands count how many times people clicked or tapped a post to see its full details, like the whole thread, the replies, or the full text. A high number usually means people were curious enough to want more of the story.
What is a good engagement rate on X?

The median engagement rate on X is 2.8%, based on Buffer's social media benchmarks. If your average is above that, you're outperforming the typical X account. If it's below, compare your post formats and timing to see where to adjust.
Yes. Buffer provides X analytics on both free and paid plans, including impressions, engagement metrics, and post-level performance, even if you don't have X Premium.
What's the difference between X analytics and Buffer analytics?

X analytics focuses only on performance within X. Buffer analytics adds averages, trends, and cross-platform insights, helping you understand how your X content performs alongside your other social channels.
How do I make a Twitter analytics report?

X doesn’t have a built-in report builder. Premium users can download post data from the Content tab and build a report themselves. In Buffer, open Insights, choose your X channel or the All Channels view and the date range, then export a branded PDF of that view to share.
What's the best time to post on X?

Buffer's analysis found that 9 a.m. on Tuesdays and 9–10 a.m. on Wednesdays performed best. Use those as a starting point, then check your own engagement patterns over time to find when your audience is most active.
How do I know if my X content is helping me grow followers?
Track follower changes alongside recent posts and campaigns. Spikes or dips often connect to specific content, timing, or increased profile visits, which can show you what makes people follow you.
